Continuation facts on large vehicles, emergency vehicles and traffic stops, plus confusable pairs among no zones, emergency responses, ticket rules and slow-moving road users; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
Because of their size and weight, large vehicles take longer to stop than cars. [A01]
Why it matters: group large vehicles; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
Following too close behind a large vehicle leaves you unseen by its driver, unable to see ahead, and with nowhere to go if it brakes suddenly. [A01]
Why it matters: group large vehicles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A01
The front no zone is about the truck's long stopping distance of at least 335 feet when loaded at 55 mph, while the rear no zone is a blind spot reaching up to 200 feet behind it. [A01]
Why it matters: group large vehicles; confusable front versus rear no zone.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A02
Pay close attention to a large vehicle's turn signals and give it plenty of room to maneuver. [A02]
Why it matters: group large vehicles; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A02
Trucks crawl in the right lane on steep hills, while near weigh stations the right lane is where trucks merge back into faster traffic; both are reasons to stay out of that lane. [A02]
Why it matters: group large vehicles; confusable hills versus weigh stations.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A03
Emergency vehicles carry sirens, flashing lights and special horns to help them move through traffic more efficiently. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A04
An officer makes a traffic stop after seeing a traffic violation or while conducting a police investigation. [A04]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: FXP0123
For a moving emergency vehicle with lights and siren on, you pull over to the road's edge, which differs from the lane change or slowdown used for a stopped one [FXP0123] [A04] [A06].
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; confusable moving versus stopped emergency vehicle.
Source: [FXP0123 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A05
At night an officer may shine a spotlight on your vehicle, so switch on the interior lights right after stopping, which lets the officer see into the vehicle. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A05
If the officer asks you to step out, stay safely away from traffic and keep your hands in plain view. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A05
Accepting a ticket does not mean you admit guilt, and contesting it happens in court rather than by arguing with the officer. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; confusable accepting a ticket versus admitting guilt.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A06
If you believe an officer acted inappropriately, report it to the officer's agency promptly; the officer's name and agency appear on the ticket, or you may ask for them. [A06]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A06
Do not make threatening motions or statements, keep your emotions in check, never interfere with the arrest of others with you and never resist arrest. [A06]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A08
Farm machinery operators may not hear you coming, while animals pulling a vehicle or carrying a rider may be frightened by a horn or a revving engine. [A08]
Why it matters: group slow-moving vehicles; confusable farm machinery versus animals.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0124]
